text:
maria_cs: FYI customer VaultPay reported streaming responses getting truncated after a brief network hiccup. They reconnect, get a short tail, then the client retries and we end up with double charge/partial outputs. Repro steps below.

sam_engineer: Can you paste the minimal repro? SDK/lang and exact flow (resume token usage)?

maria_cs: Using our JS SDK v2.1. Client opens SSE -> generation starts -> network blip -> client reconnects with resume_token and session_id. On reconnect they receive a short completion (only last 30 tokens). Client thinks it's a different completion and retries a new call. They see two billable completions for 1 prompt.

alex_repro: I reproduced locally with a proxy that drops the connection for ~700ms. Attached a short curl-based repro: 

```
# open stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: id-abc-123" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-small \
  -d '{"prompt":"Summarize X","stream":true}'
# mid-stream drop via tcpkill/proxy
# reconnect with resume_token returned earlier
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Resume-Token: rt-123" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/resume?session=ses-9
```

alex_repro: Server logs show: 
```
[runtime] sess=ses-9 resume_token=rt-123 seq_index=42 -> resumed seq_index=10 (warning)
[billing] session=ses-9 charged: tokens=130
[billing] new_request id=id-abc-123 charged: tokens=78
```

ingrid_oncall: Interesting — seq_index decreased after resume. That suggests the resumed connection served a truncated buffer (maybe returned last-chunk-only) while the original session still finished on the runtime. Client then retried, producing a second full completion. Could be a race between the streamer flushing KV cache and a fallback replay path.

sam_engineer: Do we have codepaths where a resume request can be served from a different worker with only suffix context? I thought resume verifies seq monotonicity. If seq drops we should reject resume, not issue a partial completion.

alex_repro: In my run the resume response had HTTP 200 and SSE chunk: `event: done\ndata: {"finish_reason":"stop","tokens":30}`. No explicit resume_failed. Client treats it as a full finish.

maria_cs: Customer wants to avoid double charges. They said the SDK default retry will fire on any finished stream that doesn't match their expected token count.

devbot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout 2026-07-21T03:12:10Z completed for runtime v2.7.5 on cluster-3 (no errors reported).

tim_support: Immediate workaround: ask client to include Idempotency-Key per logical prompt and suppress automatic retry if resume_token present + small token delta heuristic. Also recommend bumping SDK to check for resume_failure events.

sam_engineer: For an engineering fix, propose: 1) Make resume handler stricter — if resumed seq_index < requested offset, return 409/resume_failed (with explicit no-charge marker) rather than a 200 partial completion. 2) Add a short-lived resume lock so only the original worker that owned the KV cache can finish the original stream; other workers must return resume_failed. 3) Emit a clear audit field in billing logs linking resumed responses to original session so we can dedupe billing.

ingrid_oncall: I'll pull the traces for the customer session (span ids in the repro) and check worker-switch events. If we confirm worker handoff happened, this aligns.

maria_cs: Customer agreed to test the SDK workaround (suppress retry on resume_token) while eng works on server-side change. They've paused production traffic.

sam_engineer: Added a low-priority ticket (ENG-RUNTIME-1239) to implement stricter resume semantics + billing linkage. For now, add monitoring alert: detect "resume responded with tokens < expected" pattern and raise P2.

tim_support: Also note: update docs/SDK guide to recommend idempotency keys and jittered backoff for reconnection; include example to avoid heavy-handed immediate retries.

maria_cs: Thanks — I'll follow up with the customer after ingrid posts trace findings.

alex_repro: One more note — my local test shows that 95% of the time resume works correctly; this only triggers when worker A starts final flush after network blip and worker B answers resume using only the suffix, so it's a race. That makes it tricky to reliably test but reachable with induced proxy delay.

sam_engineer: Good context. If ingrid confirms worker handoff logs, we'll prioritize the resume-check change.

maria_cs: tagging @vaultpay account manager so they're aware. :thumbsup:
